answer: A pulse proves life only at the instant it is felt, so silence cannot be banked as standing. Each identity needs two holders outside its own terrace to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses instead of a single ring. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. An audit replays a random claim each epoch, and an unconfirmed one forfeits its relic, which cannot be pooled or resold.
